meta.title: Aeroplanes flying over India right now

prompt: Estimate the number of aeroplanes flying in India right now.

clarifications.answer: Count only commercial passenger flights that have taken off but not yet landed; ignore cargo, military, and seasonal surges.
Take the average domestic flight duration as about 2 hours (geometric mean of a 1-4 hour range).
Assume about 130 operational airports, split by size into major, medium, and small.
A supply-side approach is cleaner here: count take-offs per hour by airport type.

common_traps: Counting take-offs per hour but forgetting to multiply by average flight duration, so planes already landed are dropped.
Using full operational capacity as the live count and ignoring that airports run well below peak most of the day.
Treating one flat take-off gap for all airports instead of splitting by airport size.

anchors.1: Guesses a number with no take-off-rate reasoning.
anchors.3: Builds a take-off-rate approach but omits flight duration or the capacity adjustment.
anchors.5: Counts take-offs per hour by airport type and multiplies by average flight duration to get planes aloft.

anchors.1: One flat take-off rate for all airports.
anchors.3: Segments airports but with take-off gaps not tied to airport size.
anchors.5: Splits airports into major/medium/small with runway counts and realistic take-off gaps.

anchors.1: Errors in the per-hour-to-per-2-hour scaling; lands far outside any plausible range.
anchors.3: Reaches a number but skips the capacity haircut, landing just outside 250-750.
anchors.5: Carries the rate math cleanly and applies a capacity factor to land near 400 (250-750).

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Back-checks via daily passengers: ~400 planes x ~120 seats over the day implies a few lakh flyers, which is reasonable.
